items.label: Carbon dioxide
items.quote: Other common volcanic gases are carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, hydrogen, and fluorine.

items.label: Sulfur dioxide
items.quote: Sulfur dioxide gas can react with water droplets in the atmosphere to create acid rain, which causes corrosion and harms vegetation.

items.label: Fluorine
items.quote: Fluorine, which in high concentrations is toxic, can be adsorbed onto volcanic ash particles that later fall to the ground.

items.label: Basalt lava
items.quote: low-silica basalt lava can form fast-moving (10 to 30 miles per hour) streams

items.label: Andesite
items.quote: In contrast, flows of higher-silica andesite and dacite lava tend to be thick and sluggish, traveling only short distances from a vent.

items.label: Lava domes
items.quote: Dacite and rhyolite lavas often squeeze out of a vent to form irregular mounds called lava domes.

items.label: Pyroclastic surges
items.quote: Lower-density pyroclastic flows, called pyroclastic surges, can easily overflow ridges hundreds of feet high.

items.label: Hot ash
items.quote: High-speed avalanches of hot ash, rock fragments, and gas can move down the sides of a volcano during explosive eruptions

every item label occurs in its quote and every group label occurs in the quote or the same source paragraph (item-and-group-in-quote; the design discloses the weak-link false accept on long paragraphs — every quote is shown to the teacher)
every declared group is referenced by >= 2 items and every item groupId resolves (groups-covered)
every item has a distinct label after normalisation (distinct-items)
groups 3 (2-4) and items 8 (6-12) are within the frozen counts (counts-valid)
every number in group and item labels appears on the cited page or in the same quote (N-01) (numbers-checkable)
